diagnosis.root_cause: RADIUS still associates username C8:3A:35:26:A9:89 with the superseded ONU line ID B4:64:15:D6:DE:BB, while CRM correctly records the replacement ONU as 4C:D7:C8:C3:CC:A8. This stale line-ID mapping causes usage history to be attributed incorrectly.
evidence: The subscriber reports incorrect portal usage history while service is working, indicating an account or attribution issue rather than loss of connectivity.
The ONU is online and responding, with RX power -20.16 dBm and TX power 2.43 dBm, both within normal EPON ranges.

Seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX remains around -20 dBm, TX remains around +2.3 dBm, distance is constant at 145, and TX bias current is stable near 11.2 mA. There is no fibre, laser, or distance fault.
All seven visible peers on EPON0/5 are online, so there is no ONU, splitter, or PON-port outage.
The OLT and router are healthy, and live OLT, SNMP, and router checks succeed.
The customer VLAN is correctly provisioned: expected and actual VLAN are both 1075, so this is not a VLAN 46 or provisioning fault.
The customer has only 2 sessions in the last 24 hours with an average duration of 702 minutes, so the session pattern is normal and does not support session flapping.
RADIUS explicitly reports a line-ID conflict: RADIUS contains B4:64:15:D6:DE:BB, while CRM contains the current line ID 4C:D7:C8:C3:CC:A8 after the ONU replacement.
The old RADIUS line ID is orphaned and no longer corresponds to an installed device, directly explaining incorrect usage attribution.

remediation.action: Update the RADIUS radcheck line-ID value for username C8:3A:35:26:A9:89 to 4C:D7:C8:C3:CC:A8, remove the orphaned superseded ONU entry, synchronize CRM and RADIUS, and reauthenticate the subscriber if required. Rebuild or correct affected portal usage records where possible.

ground_truth.root_cause: The ONU was replaced on 30 August. CRM was updated with the new ONU MAC but the RADIUS lineid still carries the superseded one, so accounting records are written against a device that is no longer installed.
expected_reasoning: The customer reports incorrect usage history while service itself works
Authentication succeeds because it keys on the CPE MAC, which matches in both systems
The optical layer is healthy: RX -20.1, TX 2.4, distance constant, peers normal
crm_user_net.lineid and radcheck.lineid hold different ONU MACs for the same username
The CRM value is the installed device; the RADIUS value is a superseded one
Distance has been constant at 145 m throughout, so the physical path did not change with the swap
Accounting is therefore attributed to a device that no longer exists, which explains the portal discrepancy
This is a cross-system key mismatch, distinct from two CRM records colliding on one interface
Automated correction is unsafe here because the wrong row could be rewritten

expected_escalation.review_reason: Correcting a RADIUS lineid risks disconnecting the wrong customer and must be done by hand

distractors: Service works normally, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The complaint is about a portal display rather than connectivity
The mismatch resembles a duplicate slot conflict but is cross-system
